answer.text: release enzymes that break down protein in leaf litter
answer.line: Paragraph 6, sentence 3: many ectomycorrhizal fungi secrete enzymes that break down protein in leaf litter, freeing nitrogen locked in dead tissue.

steps: Find ectomycorrhizal next to nitrogen: paragraph 6, sentence 3.
Read the means in the same sentence. Enzymes do the unlocking: they break down protein in leaf litter.
Note the contrast that follows. Arbuscular fungi rely on nitrogen already freed into the soil.

choices.text: release enzymes that break down protein in leaf litter
choices.note: Sentence 3, nearly word for word: secrete enzymes that break down protein in leaf litter.

choices.text: capture nitrogen from air trapped inside the root mantle
choices.note: Nitrogen from air never comes up. That is outside knowledge about other partnerships.

choices.text: take up ammonium faster than a root hair can take it up
choices.note: Ammonium is named in sentence 2, but no speed comparison with root hairs appears.

choices.text: move nitrogen along the hypha as chains of polyphosphate
choices.note: Polyphosphate chains carry phosphate, sentence 1, not nitrogen. The choice puts nitrogen on phosphate's transport.

choices.text: trade nitrogen with arbuscular fungi on neighbouring roots
choices.note: The two fungal types are contrasted in sentence 3, never shown trading.
